source_text:
Διὸ ἀναζωσάμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας ὑμῶν δουλεύσατε τῷ θεῷ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, ἀπολιπόντες τὴν κενὴν ματαιολογίαν καὶ τὴν τῶν πολλῶν πλάνην, πιστεύσαντες εἰς τὸν ἐγείραντα τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόντα αὐτῷ δόξαν καὶ θρόνον ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ: ᾧ ὑπετάγη τὰ πάντα ἐπουράνια καὶ ἐπίγεια, ᾧ πᾶσα πνοὴ λατρεύει, ὃς ἔρχεται κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν, οὖ τὸ αἷμα ἐκζητήσει ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀπειθούντων αὐτῷ.
ὁ δὲ ἐγείρας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐγερεῖ, ἐὰν ποιῶμεν αὐτοῦ τὸ θέλημα καὶ πορευώμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν ἃ ἠγάπησεν, ἀπεχόμενοι πάσης ἀδικίας, πλεονεξίας, φιλαργυρίας, καταλαλιᾶς,ψευδομαρτυρίας: μὴ ἀποδιδόντες κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἢ λοιδορίαν ἀντὶ λοιδορίας ἢ γρόνθον ἀντὶ γρόνθον ἢ κατάραν ἀντὶ κατάρας:
μνημονεύοντες δὲ ὧν εἶπεν ὁ κύριος διδάσκων: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε: ἀφίετε, καὶ ἀφεθήσεται ὑμῖν: ἐλεᾶτε, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε: ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε, ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν: καὶ ὅτι μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ καὶ οἱ διωκόμενοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὑτῶν ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
thought_title: Serve God in fear and truth, remembering the Lord's teaching
orientation: Polycarp is urging the Philippians to live out the faith he has just praised, turning from empty talk to obedience and the Lord's commands.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, having girded up the loins of you, serve God in fear and truth, having abandoned the empty foolish talk and the error of the many, having believed in the one who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead and gave to him glory and a throne at his right hand: to whom all things heavenly and earthly were subjected, whom every breath serves, who comes as judge of living and dead, whose blood God will require from those disobeying him. But the one who raised him from the dead will raise us also, if we do his will and walk in his commandments and love what he loved, holding back from all wrongdoing, greed, love of money, evil speech, false witness: not giving back evil in place of evil or abuse in place of abuse or blow in place of blow or curse in place of curse: but remembering what the Lord said when teaching: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged: forgive, and it will be forgiven to you: show mercy, so that you may be shown mercy: with what measure you measure, it will be measured back to you: and that blessed are the poor and those persecuted for the sake of righteousness, because theirs is the kingdom of God.

choices.why: Keeps the compound sense of vain/empty speech without a hyphenated compound; 'foolish talk' captures the worthless chatter Polycarp warns against.
Literal rendering preserves the definite article and the genitive of source; 'the many' keeps the social scope of the warning.
Standard literal rendering of the idiom for the place of honor beside God.

choices.term: οὖ τὸ αἷμα ἐκζητήσει ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀπειθούντων αὐτῷ
choices.english: whose blood God will require from those disobeying him
choices.why: Keeps the legal force of 'require' for ἐκζητέω and the present participle 'disobeying' for ongoing refusal.
rejected: whose blood God will demand from those who disobey him
whose blood God will seek out from the disobedient

choices.term: ἀπεχόμενοι πάσης ἀδικίας, πλεονεξίας, φιλαργυρίας, καταλαλιᾶς, ψευδομαρτυρίας
choices.english: holding back from all wrongdoing, greed, love of money, evil speech, false witness
choices.why: Uses the glossary 'love of money' for φιλαργυρία; 'holding back from' keeps the middle voice sense of self-restraint.
rejected: abstaining from all injustice, covetousness, avarice, slander, false testimony

choices.english: with what measure you measure, it will be measured back to you
choices.why: Preserves the dative of instrument and the passive future with the prefix 'back' in ἀντιμετρηθήσεται.
rejected: the measure you use will be measured to you
with the measure you measure, it will be measured to you again

pass_b_english: So gird up your loins and serve God in fear and truth. Abandon the empty foolish talk and the error of the many. Believe in the one who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead and gave him glory and a throne at his right hand. To him all things in heaven and on earth were subjected. Every breath serves him. He comes as judge of the living and the dead, and God will require his blood from those who disobey him.

The one who raised him from the dead will also raise us, if we do his will and walk in his commandments and love what he loved, holding back from all wrongdoing, greed, love of money, evil speech, and false witness. Do not repay evil for evil, or insult for insult, or blow for blow, or curse for curse.

Remember what the Lord said when he taught: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged (Matthew 7:1). Forgive, and you will be forgiven (Luke 6:37). Show mercy, so that you may receive mercy (cf. Matthew 5:7). With what measure you measure, it will be measured back to you (Luke 6:38). And blessed are the poor and those persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of God (Matthew 5:3, 5:10; Luke 6:20; 'kingdom of God' follows Luke, Matthew has 'kingdom of heaven').

problems.why: The beatitude 'blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy' is Matthew 5:7, but Polycarp's saying 'ἐλεᾶτε, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε' (Show mercy, so that you may receive mercy) matches Luke 6:36 (be merciful) or is a conflation. Actually, 'ἐλεᾶτε, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε' is not exactly Matthew 5:7 (which is 'μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται'). The form 'ἐλεᾶτε, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε' appears in Luke 6:36 as 'γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες' and the preceding 'ἀφίετε, καὶ ἀφεθήσεται ὑμῖν' is Luke 6:37. The citation Matthew 5:7 for 'ἐλεᾶτε, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε' is wrong; this is a mixed citation from Luke 6:36-38.

problems.source_quote: μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ καὶ οἱ διωκόμενοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὑτῶν ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ
problems.why: Polycarp conflates 'blessed are the poor' (Luke 6:20/Matthew 5:3) with 'blessed are those persecuted for righteousness' sake' (Matthew 5:10). The citation Matthew 5:10 only covers the persecution part, not the 'poor' part. The conflation itself is in the source, but citing only Matthew 5:10 is misleading since 'the poor' comes from Matthew 5:3 or Luke 6:20. However, the instruction says 'a cited Bible reference does not match the words quoted or alluded to.' The words 'blessed are the poor' do not appear in Matthew 5:10. This is a wrong citation for the first half of the conflated saying.
